title: MSYS dollar-escape broke mkdir and wrote captures to WSL root
body: First probe used \$T inside a double-quoted wsl bash -c string; the escape collapsed, mkdir got no operand, and the six capture files landed at /apt_installed.txt-style absolute paths in the WSL root. Fix: create the dir in its own wsl call, then mv the files in. Lesson: one filesystem mutation per wsl invocation, verify the landing path before trusting a capture.

title: Excluding REMOVE-candidates from users collapsed dependency chains
body: First classifier dropped users that were themselves REMOVE-bound; sherlock-project (orphan CLI) went REMOVE and dragged stem (required only by sherlock) with it, then --check correctly failed on stem having reverse deps. Fix: fixed-point KEEP from rooted sets (imported, baseline, lane tools, self, managed, runtime) with no exclusion; dead chains fall out as REMOVE with their top named. The gate caught the exact defect it was built for.

title: Reverse-dep map keys carried version markers and underscores
body: The WSL one-liner keyed requirements by r.split()[0], so keys like jupyter-server<3,>=1.8 kept their version pins and aiohttp_socks never matched dist aiohttp-socks. 1,942 of 2,192 keys missed the in-env set. Fix: PEP 503 normalization (lowercase, [-_.] to hyphen, strip markers/extras/version) applied on load in the tool, plus self-edge drops. Lesson: normalize at the consumer, never trust the producer's key shape.

title: Path.write_text CRLF-poisoned the generated shrink scripts
body: The emitted .sh files carried CRLF because write_text translates newlines on Windows; bash died on set -u with a carriage-return option error. Fix: write_lf() helper using open(path, w, newline=\n) for all generated scripts. Lesson: every generated executable artifact needs a newline contract, and the first run of a generated script is its test.

title: Triple-nested bash quoting silently emptied the verify loop variable
body: The dpkg/pip absent-check passed through Git Bash, wsl.exe, and two bash -c layers; the loop variable arrived empty and dpkg -l with no args matched everything, printing four STILL PRESENT rows with blank names. Fix: write the verifier to a script file with printf and execute the file -- no inline nesting. Lesson: beyond two quoting layers, always use a file.

title: pygame dist was imported only by the dead module itself
body: The import scan counted import pygame inside src/azazael_pygame.py as a tree consumer of the pygame dist, but nothing imports azazael_pygame on either checkout (Windows 2026-10-11 measure plus WSL grep today: only docs/reports/pycache mention it). Fix: PIP_OVERRIDES table for dists whose sole importer is a dead module. Lesson: a dist-level scan must ask who imports the importer.

title: XPU runtime coupling is invisible to Requires-Dist
body: torch 2.14.1+xpu dlopens the intel/mkl/oneapi shared libraries without declaring them, so the fixed-point classifier marked the whole XPU stack a dead chain. Removing it would have broken the engineered replacement. Fix: RUNTIME protection set owned by device.py's XPU preference plus the /opt+15t sidecar evidence. Lesson: metadata answers declared coupling only; runtime coupling needs a named owner.

title: Project's own installed dists looked like orphans
body: azazael-*, eve-unleashed, and worm-manifest are pip-installed copies of this repo; nothing imports them as libraries and nothing requires them, so the classifier queued them for removal -- which would strand console scripts with no import error. Fix: SELF recognition (azazael prefix + exact names) rooted as self-install, enforced by --check. Lesson: the project's own artifacts are the first thing a shrink tool must learn not to eat.

title: 9P is load-bearing in WSL2; no 8p exists; severance happens on BM

An A-I-O native bridge (ssh per distro) can route tool traffic around 9P fragility but cannot remove dependence while distros boot under the MS hypervisor. True severance is BM Ubuntu (the staged runbook path). Recommendation: keep 9P for WSL lanes, add ssh as the migration-proof lane transport, do not build a custom filesystem protocol.

title: Root cause: G: kali_recovery.vhdx is a truncated prefix, not rot
body: vhdx_diag.py parse 2026-11-12: every container metadata layer is intact -- identifier vhdxfile, headers 1+2 checksums OK (seq 1256/1257), both region tables checksum OK (BAT at 3145728 len 9437184, metadata at 2097152), metadata reports blocksize 1048576 and virtual size 1024GiB, BAT fully readable with 1179648 entries. Payload: 68760 mapped blocks present (67052MiB) whose highest valid block ends exactly at EOF with a 0-byte gap; 28528 mapped blocks (27.86GiB) begin exactly at EOF and were never written. ext4 superblock magic 0xEF53 valid in block 0. Windows reports corrupted-and-unreadable because the BAT references blocks past EOF, so the host refuses the image instead of mounting with holes. Event log 2026-08-20..2026-09-05 holds zero storport/disk/exfat events and G: HealthStatus Healthy, so no hardware fault. Mechanism: metadata and BAT are written at fixed low offsets first, then data blocks stream; an exact 1MiB boundary stop with no partial trailing block means the writer terminated cleanly (space exhaustion or cancellation), not an unplugged USB which leaves a torn final block.

title: Salvage path exists but is worthless here; export tar instead of VHDX copy
body: If the truncated image ever needed salvaging: rewrite the 28528 past-EOF BAT entries to state 3 UNMAPPED and recompute the two header checksums (CRC32C over 4KiB with checksum field zeroed), which yields a read-only mountable image with holes; ext4 superblock is valid so partial recovery is plausible. Worth 0 here because live E:/Kali/ext4.vhdx is three months newer and verified healthy. Prevention for the fresh copy: use wsl --export to a single tar stream (only live data, ~25GB for a 40G estate) rather than copying a raw VHDX, check destination free space first, and verify the artifact by test-import into a throwaway distro before trusting it. A raw VHDX copy of a 1TiB virtual disk has no way to tell you it is short until mount time.

title: RESTART QUEUE block reaches only 2 of 7 lanes, has no source, and is stale
body: Measured 2026-11-12: the RESTART QUEUE section sits in C:/Users/clint/AGENTS.md and C:/Azazael/AGENTS.md and in none of the other five lane files; grep -rln over docs/agent_orders/ finds no source, so agent_orders_sync --check cannot see or correct it. Its 2026-11-07 text says freebuff 0 open, kilo 6, opencode 11 where the live board reads 100, 0 and 47, and it pins 3.15t as the only interpreter while the session-order block in the same file names 3.16t as production. This is the exact failure 07_render_handoff.md was promoted to end: prose with no owner and no check, read unprompted by agents. Remedy is promotion to a source block plus TARGETS registration, and it needs its own GO because it edits seven generated files.

title: _board.py in this tree has no release verb; surplus claims expire instead
body: Measured 2026-11-12: python _board.py rejects 'release' (choices are claim, done, block, stats, tasks, announce, max, store), so a claim taken for inspection cannot be handed back. Ten freebuff rows were claimed to read the queue and left to expire on the 30-minute lease rather than retired as work that was not done. A lane that needs to peek should read 'tasks' (claimable-only) and never 'claim'.

title: pmb MCP calls fail with Session not found after the daemon restarts under pams
body: Measured 2026-11-12 21:30: every pmb__* call returned Streamable HTTP error code -32600 'Session not found' while the stack was healthy -- a raw initialize to http://127.0.0.1:8766/mcp answered HTTP 200 with a protocolVersion result and :8765 answered the designed 401 without a token. The daemon restarted at 20:15 (pid 14564, spawned by pams _keep_pmb_warm) and the client's stdio pmb child kept a session id the new daemon never issued. Class BLOCKED: only a client restart clears it. Workaround that keeps the record: pmb.cli note/fact/learn write directly and return ULIDs (001a1d2be5815_81eccb47, 001a1d2be6051_50b394a8, 001a1d2be62be_3049795d). The gate reads PASS throughout because it probes the proxy and daemon, never the client's session.
